idea: Find the largest flow in a network in phases. Each phase builds a level graph with breadth-first search, then pushes a blocking flow along edges that go up exactly one level, using a depth-first search that never retries a dead end. When the end can no longer be reached, the flow is maximal and the cut is the edges leaving the reachable nodes.
time: O(V^2 E) in general, O(E sqrt(V)) on unit-capacity bipartite graphs
useWhen: Large flow networks where Edmonds-Karp is too slow
Matching and assignment problems turned into flow
Finding a minimum cut in a capacity network
avoidWhen: The graph is tiny and clarity matters more than speed: Edmonds-Karp is shorter to follow
Capacities are negative or the edges have costs: you need a min-cost flow method
